A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MMD research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite additions and relocation.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A.2-A.3 report original simulated multi-robot planning results, including success rates, data adherence, runtime, acceleration and generated trajectories.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulation results and adds illustrative generated trajectories in Figure 7.

M1.justification: The five MMD variants, sphere-constraint guidance, experience reuse, batch trajectory selection and local-model sequencing are retained. Newly documented data construction and possible future GBP integration do not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Empty, Highways, Conveyor and Drop-Region maps, the tiled 2 × 2 and 3 × 3 environments, and circle/weave scenarios. Figure 7 illustrates retained coverage; decentralized and dynamic-environment planning remain future directions.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain MPD-Composite, A*Data-ECBS, A*-ECBS and the same MMD variants. Newly cited GBP and RRT-Connect are not added evaluation baselines.

E3.justification: The existing experiment counts, runtime limits, adherence metrics, robot settings and staggered-start procedure match. The 64-point trajectory format and additional map details are newly disclosed settings, without evidence of a revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 7 adds qualitative cases showing single-robot trajectories following local motion patterns across tiled maps. Existing constraining-strategy, congestion, scalability and failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Trial-count reporting is unchanged. Neither version adds seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1-2 and the results displayed in Figures 2-6 are unchanged. Figure 7 adds large-map MMD trajectory examples described as having perfect data adherence, providing limited additional qualitative outcomes.

T1.justification: Section 5 qualifies the guarantee attributed to coupled sampling-based planning from completeness to probabilistic completeness. MMD's mathematics otherwise retains its substance: shortened Equation (1) and the explicit large-map adherence average restate existing content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of collision-free multi-robot planning from single-robot data, comparison of five MMD variants, and scaling through local-model composition. Wording changes do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: New A.1.1 substantially expands applicability limitations concerning known obstacle motions, faithful execution, offline planning and communication, and discusses decentralized/windowed extensions. A.8 adds practitioner recommendations, while Section 4.2 adds a runtime/adherence interpretation. The earlier explicit fixed-duration limitation in Section 6 is removed.

D1.justification: New A.7 documents 64-point trajectories with velocities and dataset construction using skill subpaths, RRT-Connect, B-splines and optimization. A.5.1 specifies tiled-map composition and scoring, and the introduction adds a project-page link. These substantially expand documentation of the existing data pipeline and setup.

R1.justification: Section 5 revises MRMP positioning, and new A.1.1 substantially extends comparison with decentralized/windowed planning, especially GBP. Citations add Patwardhan et al. (2023), Okumura et al. (2019), Van Den Berg et al. (2011), Nilsson (1982), and Kuffner and LaValle (2000); Chen et al. (2021) and Solis et al. (2021) are removed.

P1.justification: v2 compresses the contribution bullets, locally rewrites method explanations, experimental discussion and related work, introduces Section 4.2.1, and adds appendix subsections. Author affiliations and publication headers change, while most existing prose and the main section sequence remain.

P2.justification: Figure 7 adds six map-and-trajectory panels. Figures 5-6 and Table 2 are relocated, captions for Figures 3-4 are shortened, and conference headers are added. Existing plot graphics and table structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: The added data-generation recipe, map documentation and applicability discussion make v2 easier to understand and implement. These provide a limited net quality gain, partly offset by removal of v1's explicit fixed-duration warning. Training specifics still largely refer readers to the cited procedure and code, and the benchmark evidence remains unchanged.
